To analyze the results, the following two hybrid process cases with RF/US integration were identified: (i) Hybrid Case 1: Additional electricity requirement resulting from the integration is met by onsite cogeneration of steam and electricity, (ii) Hybrid Case 2: Additional electricity requirement is met using purchased electricity. For the preliminary analysis, a 10% displacement of steam from the integration of RF/US was considered, with initially an assumed leverage factor of 4 units of steam energy reduction offset by 1 unit of electrical energy. Later experiments revealed this is too optimistic an assessment of how RF and US would perform. Still, this assumption translated to a net energy intensity reduction 52 DE-EE0009395 of 6.3%. A key assumption was that a majority of the onsite steam requirement (~88%) is met by biogenic fuels with zero emission intensity based on 2017 literature studies (not MECS data which was more dated). Natural gas and fuel oil were considered as swing fuels to accommodate the change in energy requirement of the drying process from RF/US integration. For these values, Hybrid Case 1 showed the maximum reduction in CO emission intensity (83% nationwide average for boxboard) 2 and fuel consumption (4% nationwide average for carton [box] board) from the base case. Since the additional electricity requirement in Hybrid Case 2 is met using purchased electricity, the indirect CO emissions resulting from the carbon footprint of the purchased electricity from the 2 grid formed a significant portion of the total CO emission intensity. This resulted in higher CO 2 2 emission intensity of Hybrid Case 2 compared to Hybrid Case 1 (56% nationwide average reduction from base-case for carton board). Figure 40 demonstrates these results for carton board. Figure 40: Average boxboard CO emission intensity for different cases 2 At the end of 2022, this analysis resulted in the expected reduction in carbon emissions using data on the paper grade, production capacity and technical age for paper mills across the U.S. which was obtained from industry representatives (APPTI) (Figure 41). The indirect CO emissions of Hybrid Case 2 also vary based on the geographical region and the 2 year of study. As the grid gets greener, the indirect emission intensity decreases. In 2040, the average emission intensity reduction of Hybrid Case 2 compared to base-case is 65% for boxboard, with the highest reduction observed in the Northwest and Pacific regions of the United States. Figures 40 and 41 demonstrate this result. Similarly, the fuel consumption of the process decreases from 2022 to 2040 due to the decrease in indirect fuel consumption. The resulting net average reduction in fuel consumption from base-case is 3% for boxboard in 2040. 53 DE-EE0009395 Figure 41: Reduction in CO emissions from RF/US integration for Hybrid case 2 for boxboard 2 mills and scope 2 emission intensity for 2040.
